sources.title: Local Japanese unnumbered promo WotC catalog: Emperor of the Crystal Tower theatrical release pair

claims.text: Bulbapedia card pages place the Japanese theatrical-screening availability for Hitmontop and Igglybuff on July 8, 2000, while the local raw source group preserves the theatrical-release note under source indices 182 and 183.
The local raw source group models two source-index rows for this theatrical route: Hitmontop 182 and Igglybuff 183.
Bulbapedia and PokeBoon describe the Japanese route as a theatrical-screening / movie-attendee promotional card distribution for Emperor of the Crystal Tower: Entei.
PokeBoon and the Bulbapedia card pages identify Atsuko Nishida for Hitmontop and Kagemaru Himeno for Igglybuff; the local raw source rows themselves do not provide illustrator authority.
This normal-size theatrical pair must be kept separate from Crystal Tower's Entei, a CoroCoro August 2000 jumbo insert deepened elsewhere in the catalog-history layer.

The pair matters because it turns a movie outing into a small two-card Johto souvenir: Hitmontop carries motion and Fighting-type novelty, while Igglybuff carries baby-Pokemon softness beside the Entei movie machine.

Agents should preserve source indices 182/183, theatrical-route context, artist split, movie-attendee text, and non-equivalence with the CoroCoro Entei jumbo, ordinary Neo-era Hitmontop/Igglybuff, and English Wizards Black Star listings before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Entei at the theater door — Hitmontop and Igglybuff as movie souvenirs
narrative.why_it_matters: This pair is Pokemon as an outing you could hold. The third movie made the Crystal Tower enormous on screen, but the theater gift was small and intimate: Hitmontop spinning with new-Johto energy, Igglybuff softening the route into baby-Pokemon charm. It is not just a promo pair; it is a receipt from a summer movie moment.

narrative.human_title: Movie Hitmontop — the spin at the theater door
narrative.why_it_matters: Hitmontop feels exactly right for a movie-attendee promo: motion, novelty, and Johto-era freshness arriving in a kid's hands after the Crystal Tower filled the screen. Atsuko Nishida's credit gives the card a clean artist lane, but the real identity is the route. Without the theater story, it is only another Hitmontop.

narrative.human_title: Movie Igglybuff — the soft card beside the tower
narrative.why_it_matters: Igglybuff is the little emotional counterspell to the Crystal Tower. The movie apparatus is huge: Entei, Unown, theater crowds, summer promotion. Then this tiny baby Pokemon appears as something you could take home. Kagemaru Himeno's lane makes that softness feel intentional, but again the route is the identity.
